results.title: Triple intersections with conjugates

results.title: Subgroup generated by the triple intersections of least order
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Family of local exponents
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A local-exponent family indexed by a type $\iota$ is a function $m : \iota \to \mathbb{R}$, the local Langlands exponents, with $0 \le m(i) \le 1/2$ for every $i \in \iota$.

results.title: Exponent set of a local-exponent family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a local-exponent family $F$ indexed by a type $\iota$, with local exponents $m(i)$ for $i \in \iota$, the exponent set of $F$ is the set of real numbers $\{0\} \cup \{m(i) : i \in \iota\}$.

results.title: Ramanujan exponent of a local-exponent family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Ramanujan exponent of a local-exponent family $F$ with local exponents $m(i)$, $i \in \iota$, is the supremum of the set $\{0\} \cup \{m(i) : i \in \iota\}$. It is the supremum of the local exponents when $\iota$ is nonempty, and $0$ when $\iota$ is empty.

results.title: Admissibility of an exponent for a local-exponent family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A local-exponent family $F$ is admissible at a real number $\delta$ (Hypothesis $H_2(\delta)$ for $F$) when every local exponent $m_i$ of $F$ ($i \in \iota$) is at most $\delta$.

results.title: Generalized Ramanujan conjecture for a family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A local-exponent family $F$ satisfies the Generalized Ramanujan conclusion when every local exponent $m_i$ of $F$ ($i \in \iota$) is zero.

results.title: Local exponents are bounded by the Ramanujan exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every local-exponent family $F$ and every index $i$, the local exponent $m_i$ of $F$ at $i$ is at most the Ramanujan exponent of $F$.

results.title: The Ramanujan exponent is admissible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every local-exponent family $F$, $F$ is admissible at its Ramanujan exponent: every local exponent of $F$ is at most the Ramanujan exponent of $F$.

results.title: Admissible exponents bound the Ramanujan exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a local-exponent family and let $\delta \ge 0$ be a real number. If $\delta$ is admissible for $F$, that is, every local exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$, then the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$.

results.title: Admissibility is a bound by the Ramanujan exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every local-exponent family $F$ and every real $\delta \ge 0$, $F$ is admissible at $\delta$ if and only if the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$.

results.title: The Ramanujan exponent vanishes exactly in the tempered case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every local-exponent family $F$, the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ is $0$ if and only if $F$ satisfies the generalized Ramanujan conclusion, that is, every local exponent of $F$ is $0$.

results.title: Admissible exponents of a local-exponent family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a local-exponent family $F$ with local exponents $m_i$ ($i \in \iota$), the set of admissible exponents of $F$ is the set of real numbers $\delta \ge 0$ such that $F$ is admissible at $\delta$, that is, $m_i \le \delta$ for every index $i$.

results.title: The Ramanujan exponent is the infimum of the admissible exponents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every local-exponent family $F$, the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ equals the infimum of the admissible exponents of $F$, that is, of the set of real numbers $\delta \ge 0$ such that every local exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$.

results.title: Selberg family of archimedean exponents

results.title: Exceptional eigenvalues bound Selberg-dominating exponents from below

results.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, we have $(x^{\oplus i})^{\oplus i} = x$.

results.title: Flipping a coordinate is an involution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the map $x \mapsto x^{\oplus i}$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, which flips the $i$-th coordinate, is an involution: applying it twice gives the identity.

results.title: A coordinate flip moves every point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ obtained from $x$ by flipping its $i$-th coordinate is different from $x$.

results.title: Sign of a negated Boolean value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, the sign of its negation is the negative of its sign: $\sigma(\lnot b) = -\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

results.title: Coordinate signs are nonzero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ (equal to $1$ for true and $-1$ for false) is nonzero.

results.title: Coordinate signs have absolute value one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$, which is $1$ for true and $-1$ for false, satisfies $|\sigma(b)| = 1$.

results.title: Flipping a coordinate in a Fourier character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i < n$, and write $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped. Then the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = -\chi_S(x)$ if $i \in S$, and $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = \chi_S(x)$ if $i \notin S$.

results.title: Flipping a coordinate preserves sums over the cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f$ a function from the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ to $M$, and $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For a point $x$ of the cube write $x^{\oplus i}$ for the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Then $\sum_x f(x^{\oplus i}) = \sum_x f(x)$, both sums ranging over all points $x$ of the cube.

results.title: Averages are invariant under flipping a coordinate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid that is a module over the nonnegative rationals, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates to $M$, and let $i < n$. Writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped, the uniform average of $f(x^{\oplus i})$ over all points $x$ of the cube equals the uniform average of $f(x)$.

results.title: Uniform average over the Boolean cube as a sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients as averages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is the average of $f(x) \chi_S(x)$ over all points $x$ of the cube, $\hat f(S) = \mathbb{E}_x [f(x) \chi_S(x)]$, where $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients as sums over the cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_x f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where the sum runs over all points $x$ of the cube and $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.

results.title: Average over the Boolean cube as the empty Fourier coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)$ of $f$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(\emptyset)$ of $f$ at the empty set.

results.title: Orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ and $T$ be subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\chi_S$ and $\chi_T$ be their Fourier characters. Then $\sum_x \chi_S(x) \chi_T(x)$, the sum ranging over all points $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, equals $2^n$ if $S = T$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Sum of a Boolean cube character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the sum of the Fourier character $\chi_S$ over all points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ equals $2^n$ if $S$ is empty and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Dual orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y$ be points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\chi_S$ be the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \chi_S(x) \chi_S(y)$, the sum ranging over all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, equals $2^n$ if $x = y$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Fourier inversion on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $x$ be a point of the cube. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\hat f(S)$ be the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $\chi_S$ the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \hat f(S) \chi_S(x) = f(x)$, the sum ranging over all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: Plancherel's identity on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all functions $f, g : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f g$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the products of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) g(x) = \sum_S \hat f(S) \hat g(S)$.

results.title: Parseval's identity on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f^2$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)^2 = \sum_S \hat f(S)^2$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients determine the function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates have the same Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S) = \hat g(S)$ at every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, then $f = g$.

results.title: Additivity of Fourier coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $f + g$ at $S$ is the sum of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$: $\widehat{f + g}(S) = \hat f(S) + \hat g(S)$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients of a difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the Fourier coefficient of $f - g$ at $S$ is $\widehat{f - g}(S) = \hat f(S) - \hat g(S)$.

results.title: Homogeneity of Fourier coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $c$, every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $c f$ at $S$ is $c$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$: $\widehat{c f}(S) = c \hat f(S)$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients of a constant function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $c$ and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates is $c$ if $S = \emptyset$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Fourier coefficients of a character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all sets $S$ and $T$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the Fourier character $\chi_T$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, $\chi_T(x) = \prod_{i \in T} \sigma(x_i)$ with $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$, is $1$ if $T = S$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Uniqueness of the Fourier expansion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real numbers $a_T$ indexed by the sets $T \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $g(x) = \sum_T a_T \chi_T(x)$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$, where $\chi_T$ is the Fourier character of $T$. Then for every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $S$ is $\hat g(S) = a_S$.

Write $\hat f(S)$ and $\hat g(S)$ for the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at a set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates. results.title: Influence of a coordinate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of $i$ on $f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[\big((f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})) / 2\big)^2\big]$, where the expectation is over $x$ uniform on the cube and $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.

results.title: Total influence on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is the sum of the influences of its $n$ coordinates, $\mathrm{I}[f] = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$, where $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x \left[\left(\frac{f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})}{2}\right)^2\right]$, $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped and $\mathbb{E}_x$ is the uniform average over the…

results.title: Variance on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, its variance under the uniform distribution is $\mathrm{Var}[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[(f(x) - \mathbb{E}_y[f(y)])^2\big]$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$ denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.

results.title: Influences are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ of coordinate $i$ on $f$ satisfies $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge 0$.

results.title: Total influence is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is nonnegative.

results.title: Variance on the Boolean cube is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution is at least $0$.

results.title: Constant functions have zero influence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $c$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.

results.title: Constant functions have zero total influence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has total influence $0$.

results.title: Constant functions have zero variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has variance $0$ under the uniform distribution.

results.title: Influence of a Boolean function as a flip probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ that takes only the values $1$ and $-1$, and let $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ equals the probability, for $x$ uniform on the cube, that $f(x^{\oplus i}) \ne f(x)$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.

results.title: Fourier formula for influence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \sum_{S \ni i} \hat f(S)^2$, where $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and the sum runs over the sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain $i$.

results.title: Variance in terms of Fourier coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution equals $\sum_{S \neq \emptyset} \hat f(S)^2$, where the sum runs over the nonempty sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.

results.title: Variance as mean square minus squared mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution equals $\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)^2] - (\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)])^2$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$ denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution is at most the total influence of $f$: $\mathrm{Var}[f] \le I[f]$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $\rho$, every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of $T_\rho f$, the noise operator with parameter $\rho$ applied to $f$, is $\widehat{T_\rho f}(S) = \rho^{|S|} \hat f(S)$.

results.title: The noise operator $T_1$ is the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator with $\rho = 1$ fixes $f$: $T_1 f = f$.

results.title: Semigroup property of the noise operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$, applying the noise operator $T_\sigma$ and then $T_\rho$ to $f$ gives $T_{\rho\sigma} f$: $T_\rho(T_\sigma f) = T_{\rho\sigma} f$.

results.title: The noise operator preserves the mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $\rho$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the uniform average over the cube of $T_\rho f$, the image of $f$ under the noise operator with parameter $\rho$, equals the uniform average of $f$.

results.title: Characters are eigenfunctions of the noise operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $\rho$ and every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ maps the Fourier character $\chi_S$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to the function $x \mapsto \rho^{|S|} \chi_S(x)$, so $\chi_S$ is an eigenfunction of $T_\rho$ with eigenvalue $\rho^{|S|}$.

results.title: The noise operator fixes constants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $\rho$ and every real number $c$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ maps the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to itself.

results.title: Positivity of the noise operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $\rho$ with $|\rho| \le 1$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ on the Boolean cube maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions: if $f$ is a real function on the cube with $f(y) \ge 0$ for every point $y$, then $T_\rho f(x) \ge 0$ for every point $x$ of the cube.

results.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts on an input word $w$ when its run from the initial configuration on $w$ (the start state, with $w$ written from the head position rightwards on an otherwise blank tape) reaches, in finitely many steps (possibly none), a configuration in the halting state.

results.title: Halting from a configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts from a configuration $c$ when its run from $c$ reaches, in finitely many steps (possibly none), a configuration in the halting state.

results.title: Halting on an input is halting from the initial configuration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts on an input word $w$ if and only if $M$ halts from the initial configuration on $w$.

results.title: A machine that produces an output halts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a single-tape Turing machine $M$ outputs a word $w'$ on an input word $w$, then $M$ halts on $w$.

results.title: Single-tape Turing machines are deterministic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$, every configuration of $M$ has at most one successor under the transition relation of $M$.

results.title: Halting configurations are exactly those without a successor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$ and a configuration $c$ of $M$, one step of $M$ from $c$ gives no configuration if and only if $c$ is in the halting state.

results.title: Halting from a configuration is normalizability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine and $c$ a configuration of $M$. Then $M$ halts from $c$ if and only if $c$ is normalizable for the transition relation of $M$, that is, the run of $M$ from $c$ reaches, in finitely many steps (possibly none), a configuration that has no successor.

results.title: Halting from a configuration is invariant along a run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine and let $a$ and $b$ be configurations of $M$ such that the run of $M$ from $a$ reaches $b$ in finitely many steps (possibly none). Then $M$ halts from $a$ if and only if $M$ halts from $b$.

results.title: Configurations with the same successor halt together
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine and let $a$ and $b$ be configurations of $M$ that have the same successor, or that both have no successor. Then $M$ halts from $a$ if and only if $M$ halts from $b$.

results.title: Distinct words give distinct tapes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The map sending a word $w$ to the tape that holds $w$ from the head position rightwards, every other cell blank, is injective.

results.title: Outputs are unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a single-tape Turing machine $M$ outputs the word $l_1$ on the input $l$ and also outputs the word $l_2$ on the input $l$, then $l_1 = l_2$. Here $M$ outputs a word $w$ on $l$ when its run from the initial configuration on $l$ halts with exactly $w$ on the tape, every other cell blank and the head on the first symbol of $w$ (an all-blank tape if $w$ is empty).

results.title: Guard priority condition on active endpoints
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A guard precedes every other active owned endpoint. Transferred payloads are included in ownership until transfer; no enabled edge is assumed.

results.title: A guard owning only its own endpoint satisfies the condition

results.title: Adding a completed role preserves the guard condition

results.title: Restoring the bound pair preserves ranked typing

results.title: Reverse scope extrusion preserves ranked typing

results.title: Endpoint substitution preserves ranked typing

results.title: Progress at reachable states of closed ranked networks
results.caption: Theorem

results.summary: `#histories * 2^{n-1} = n! (n - 1)!`, i.e. there are `n! (n - 1)! / 2^{n-1}` ranked labeled histories of `n` labeled genes (Edwards 1970).

results.title: Random joining
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Random joining (Edwards 1970; Kingman 1982): the pair merging at each step is uniform among the current `(n - i).choose 2` pairs and independent of the earlier steps. Kingman (1982) shows that this is the law of the tree topology of the coalescent.

results.title: Every ranked history is equally likely under random joining
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under random joining each history has probability `∏_{k=2}^n C(k, 2)⁻¹`.

results.title: Each ranked labeled history has probability `2^{n-1} / (n! (n - 1)!)`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Each ranked labeled history has probability `2^{n-1} / (n! (n - 1)!)` under random joining (Edwards 1970; Tajima 1983).
